title: 'Presence: animate things leaving'
description: Keep a view or a keyed list row mounted until its leave animation finishes, including nested children and rows that return mid-exit.

A leave animation needs an element to still exist. `@if` and `@for` remove nodes synchronously, so by the time `moveLeave` could run, the node is gone — the directive is not broken, there is simply nothing left. Presence directives own the lifetime instead: they hold the view, wait for every registered leave animation, and only then let Angular remove it.

## A single view: `*movePresence`

:::code panel.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-panel',
  imports: [MovePresenceDirective, MoveEnterDirective, MoveLeaveDirective],
  template: `
    <ng-container *movePresence="open()">
      <aside moveEnter="fade-left" moveLeave="fade-right">Settings</aside>
    </ng-container>
  `,
})
export class Panel {
  protected readonly open = signal(true);
}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/presence.ts#L10-L21)

[`MovePresenceDirective`](/docs/reference/move-presence-directive) waits for **all** descendants that registered a leave animation, including nested ones.

## A keyed list: `*movePresenceFor`

[`MovePresenceForDirective`](/docs/reference/move-presence-for-directive) is the list counterpart: each row stays mounted while it leaves, and a row that returns mid-exit is revived instead of duplicated.

:::code rows.ts

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-rows',
  imports: [MovePresenceForDirective, MoveEnterDirective, MoveLeaveDirective],
  template: `
    <ul>
      <li
        *movePresenceFor="let row of rows(); trackBy: byId"
        moveEnter="fade-up"
        moveLeave="fade-down"
      >
        {{ row.name }}
      </li>
    </ul>
  `,
})
export class Rows {
  protected readonly rows = signal<readonly Row[]>([{ id: 1, name: 'First' }]);
  protected readonly byId = (_: number, row: Row) => row.id;
}
```

[View source](https://github.com/Andersseen/angular-movement/blob/main/src/docs-snippets/presence.ts#L30-L48)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Track by a **stable identity**, never by index. With `track $index` Angular reuses DOM nodes, so reordering does not replay enter animations and exit animations attach to the wrong row.

Plain `@for (row of rows(); track row.id)` is still right when rows never need an exit animation.

## Exit variants

With `moveVariants`, `moveExitVariant` names the variant that plays inside `*movePresence` before removal. With `[moveAnimation]`, use its `exit` state.
